newsitem.title: USA: Accused zucchini bandit back to court.
newsitem.headline: Accused zucchini bandit back to court.

text.p: New York's "Zucchini Bandit," who is accused of using a cucumber-shaped squash as a weapon in a mugging, is headed back to court.
Carlos Diaz faces a fourth trial in the case after three earlier trials ended in mistrial or hung juries. Proceedings were slated for Friday in State Supreme Court in Queens.

Diaz, 28, was arrested in April 1995 after restaurant worker Oscar Leal identified him as the man who ordered him to hand over his wristwatch and $20 or he would shoot. Police recovered the alleged stolen goods -- and the zucchini they say Diaz hid in a paper bag and pretended was a loaded gun.
After the first three trials were inconclusive, the Queens District Attorney's office opted in an unusual move to try him a fourth time.
"It's preposterous. Their judgment has been warped by a zucchini," defence attorney Steven Silberblatt said at the end of Diaz' third trial in August.
"You take enough shots at a guy and you're bound to hit him," he said. "It's time to move on to other vegetables."
But prosecutors take a different view of Diaz, who has a record of felonies. They note he also faces robbery charges in a second case in which he allegedly robbed a cab driver with a real gun.
"The second case underscores what we have been saying all along to justify retrying him," prosecutor Kirk Bartley said. "He's a dangerous individual and if let loose he'll harm the community."

In the second case, Diaz allegedly held up a livery cab driver at gunpoint and took his wallet and his taxi. He was arrested hours later after he allegedly tried to sell the taxi's radio to his victim's co-worker.
His trial on that case is set to begin next month.
